VERIFY LIST — every OCCDS/ADaM specific this session intends to assert.

--- Structure, and why OCCDS is not BDS ---

O1 [OCCDS v1.1 §1.1.2, Principles 1-3] OCCDS applies when: (1) there is
   NO need for AVAL/AVALC because occurrences are COUNTED, not
   measured; (2) a dictionary hierarchy is typically used and remapping
   it to PARAM/*CAT would lose its structure and meaning; (3) data
   content is typically not modified for analysis. Also §1.1.2:
   "typically, findings data fit nicely into BDS, and events and
   interventions fit nicely into OCCDS."

O2 [OCCDS v1.1 §3.2] OCCDS is explicitly different from BDS: "There is
   no PARAM nor AVAL, for example." Some BDS variables may still be
   used in OCCDS, and some OCCDS variables (e.g. TRTEMFL) may be used
   outside OCCDS.

O3 [OCCDS v1.1 §3.1.2] Datasets of SubClass ADVERSE EVENT must have
   Class = OCCURRENCE DATA STRUCTURE; structure is usually 1 record per
   record in the corresponding SDTM domain; SDTM input is always AE
   (plus SUPPAE, FA, ADSL); MH/CE data are NOT included in the
   SubClass. And the escape hatch: "Not all OCCDS datasets that contain
   adverse event data will necessarily be of SubClass ADVERSE EVENT."

--- The MedDRA constraint (author-approved framing) ---

O4 [OCCDS v1.1 §3.2.3] For SubClass ADVERSE EVENT it is REQUIRED that
   all levels of the MedDRA primary path — SOC, HLGT, HLT, LLT, PT — be
   included. "For other OCCDS datasets, these variables are recommended
   ... but not required." GLPX AEDECOD is null for all 389 rows
   (MedDRA is licensed; the course never fakes coded terms), so the
   SubClass is structurally unreachable and this ADAE is built as
   Class = OCCURRENCE DATA STRUCTURE.

O5 [OCCDS v1.1 §1.1.2, Principle 2 parenthetical] THE KEY SANCTION —
   the IG addresses our exact case directly: "Data for a particular
   study that could have been coded but was not should use this
   structure because analysis results are similar, and this will allow
   analysis programming to work the same way." So building ADAE as
   OCCDS without coded terms is not a workaround; it is what the guide
   says to do. NOTE: this is a stronger and more precise warrant than
   the §3.1.2 escape hatch I cited when proposing the split — lead with
   O5, support with O3.

O6 [OCCDS v1.1 §3.2, Table 3.2.6.1 vs Table 3.2.6.2] The occurrence
   flags split cleanly along the MedDRA line, and the IG's own table
   titles do the work:
     Table 3.2.6.1 (general): AOCCFL (1st within subject) and AOCCIFL
       (1st max severity within subject) -> BUILDABLE here; AOCCPFL and
       AOCCPIFL need --DECOD (PT) -> NOT buildable.
     Table 3.2.6.2 "MedDRA Occurrence Flag Variables": AOCCSFL (1st per
       SOC), AOCCSIFL -> NOT buildable.
   All are Core = Perm. Taught as cited fact; never fabricated.
   CORRECTION TO MY OWN SPLIT MEMO: I told the author only AOCCFL was
   buildable. AOCCIFL is buildable too — it keys on maximum severity,
   which GLPX has (AESEV), not on a coded term.

--- Treatment emergence (the centrepiece) ---

O7 [OCCDS v1.1 §3.2, Table 3.2.5.3] TRTEMFL "Treatment Emergent
   Analysis Flag", Char, Core = Cond (Req for SubClass ADVERSE EVENT).
   Example derivation, verbatim: "If ADSL.TRTSDT<=ASTDT<=ADSL.TRTEDT +
   x days then TRTEMFL='Y'", where x is producer-defined and "often
   incorporates the known half-life of the drug". For non-SubClass
   datasets it is "conditional on whether the concept of treatment
   emergent is a key feature of the analysis" — it is the key feature
   here, so the condition is met.
   AUTHOR'S QUESTION ANSWERED: TRTEMFL is a PURE TIMING derivation —
   ASTDT against ADSL.TRTSDT/TRTEDT. No coded term, no MedDRA
   dependency anywhere in its definition. Nothing about what is
   buildable changes.

O8 [OCCDS v1.1 §3.2, Table 3.2.5.3] AETRTEM is the SDTM treatment-
   emergent flag from SUPPAE (QNAM="AETRTEM"), Core = Perm. "TRTEMFL
   may differ from AETRTEM due to different definitions, date
   imputation, and other analysis rules." GLPX has no SUPPAE, so
   AETRTEM is absent — stated, not faked. Same ADaM-re-derives-flags
   lesson as ADSL's population flags (ADaMIG v1.3, §3.5).

--- Timing ---

O9 [OCCDS v1.1 §3.2, Table 3.2.4.1] ASTDT = "Analysis Start Date",
   Core = Cond, "created from converting XX.--STDTC from character ISO
   8601 format to numeric date format, applying imputation rules if
   specified in the statistical analysis plan (SAP) or metadata".
   AENDT likewise from --ENDTC. --STDTC/--ENDTC are themselves copied
   in for traceability.

O10 [OCCDS v1.1 §3.2, Table 3.2.4.1] ASTDTF "Analysis Start Date
    Imputation Flag", Char, codelist DATEFL, Core = Cond — "conditional
    on whether ASTDT (or the date part of ASTDTM) was imputed".
    GLPX D4: subject 103-199 has a NULL AESTDTC. We do NOT impute it,
    so ASTDT is null and ASTDTF stays null — and TRTEMFL cannot be
    evaluated for that record. This is the session's honest-missingness
    example, mirroring ADSL's four null AGEs.

O11 [OCCDS v1.1 §3.2, Table 3.2.4.1] ASTDY "Analysis Start Relative
    Day", Core = Cond, derivation given: "ASTDT - ADSL.TRTSDT + 1 if
    ASTDT >= ADSL.TRTSDT, else ASTDT - ADSL.TRTSDT" — the SAME no-day-0
    rule as SDTMIG v3.4 §4.4.4, but anchored to ADSL.TRTSDT rather than
    DM.RFSTDTC. AESTDY may be copied alongside: "ASTDY may differ from
    --STDY due to date imputation and the option in ADaM to use a
    reference date other than SDTM's RFSTDTC."

--- Identifiers, the ADSL merge, traceability ---

O12 [OCCDS v1.1 §3.2.2, Table 3.2.2.1] STUDYID, USUBJID Req; SUBJID,
    SITEID Perm — and sourced ADSL.SUBJID / ADSL.SITEID, i.e. from
    ADSL, not from the SDTM domain.

O13 [OCCDS v1.1 §3.2.2] Row identifiers give datapoint traceability:
    where rows come from a single SDTM domain, --SEQ (here AESEQ)
    supplies it all; SRCDOM + SRCSEQ are the alternative for
    multi-domain sources. Explicit: BDS's SRCVAR is NOT used in OCCDS,
    because SRCVAR names the variable deriving AVAL/AVALC and those do
    not exist here.

O14 [OCCDS v1.1 §3.2.1] "Merge any subject-level variables needed for
    analysis or reference." And the denominator warning, which is the
    reason ADSL exists: "only subjects with a record in an input SDTM
    domain would have a record in the analysis dataset ... population
    indicators and denominator counts for percentages [should] be
    derived from ADSL and not from the occurrence analysis dataset."
    GLPX: 389 AE rows over 262 subjects, but the safety denominator is
    400 from ADSL. Single most consequential sentence in the session.

--- Severity ---

O15 [OCCDS v1.1 §3.2, Table 3.2.5.2] --SEV copied from AE.AESEV; ASEV
    "Analysis Severity/Intensity" is the analysis version and ASEVN its
    numeric counterpart (Core = Perm, values 1/2/3). The IG's worked
    example maps MILD/MODERATE/SEVERE to Mild/Moderate/Severe. The
    same-name rule still governs (ADaMIG v1.3, §3.1.1 item 3): AESEV
    must stay the SDTM value; any recoding goes in ASEV.
    VERIFY AT PROSE TIME: confirm the exact table number for the
    severity block (read as 3.2.5.2, adjacent to 3.2.5.3 Adverse Events
    Indicator Variables) before citing it.

--- Version pairing (author-supplied; must be disclosed) ---

O16 OCCDS v1.1 front matter states it is "based on the Analysis Data
    Model (ADaM) v2.1 and the ADaM Implementation Guide (ADaMIG) v1.2",
    and it cites SDTMIG v3.3 and ADaMIG v1.2 section numbers
    throughout. Author-confirmed disclosure to make in prose: v1.1
    references v1.2/v3.3 in its front matter but IS CDISC's designated
    companion to ADaMIG v1.3 — the ADaMIG v1.3 page states OCCDS "is
    described in ADaM OCCDS v1.1", and the v1.3 Release Package ships
    it. A small teaching point about staggered CDISC versioning.

### How to Use the Code in This Session

Every code chunk below is written so you can copy it into your R
console (or an R script) and run it yourself, in the order shown. Run R
from the project root, as in earlier sessions.

This session reads `data/sdtm/ae.csv` and — for the first time —
`data/adam/adsl.csv`. Treatment emergence cannot be decided without the
treatment dates ADSL carries, which is why ADSL came first.
:::

## When Do You Use This? {#sec-adae}

TODO (prose pass): scenarios — a safety table needs every event
classified as treatment emergent or not; a reviewer asks which subjects
had their first severe event while on drug; someone needs adverse-event
percentages with the *right* denominator. Ends with the bold question:
**what does an analysis dataset look like when there is nothing to
measure — only occurrences to count?** Builds on [ADaM
Concepts](adam-concepts.qmd), [ADSL](adsl.qmd) and
